challenge.method: Tested whether the README covers this public-domain tool's legal text, whether the file merely explains how someone else can dedicate a Work, and whether the trademark reservation displaces the stated copyright terms.
challenge.results: The README includes CC0 among its public-domain tools and expressly dedicates legal-tool text. The pinned file is the legal code in plaintext. Its own waiver language would not alone establish Creative Commons' decision to dedicate the document itself. The adjacent reservation governs uses of marks and logos and leaves the stated copyright basis for an exact copy intact.

limitations: The claim concerns a copy retaining the identified 7,048 plaintext bytes. Exactness bounds the assessed case.
Creative Commons separately reserves trademark and logo uses subject to the exceptions in its Trademark section. Other repository assets have their own terms.
Rights in a separate Work to which someone applies CC0 depend on that application and the rights the Affirmer holds.
reasoning: The pinned repository's Copying and licenses section dedicates “the text of the Creative Commons legal tools” under CC0 1.0 Universal. At that same commit, the identified file contains the English legal code of a tool the README expressly lists. The publisher's dedication therefore covers copyright reuse of that file, including exact reproduction and distribution, both rights identified in section 1(i). The file's title establishes which text is being copied. The README supplies the publisher's operative copying terms.
